messages:
maria: FYI customer on region-us reports JSON-mode streaming responses getting cut mid-object after a gRPC client reset. Parser error: 'unexpected end of JSON input'. They say this happens ~10% of requests and they were billed for partial responses :/
kevin: Do we know if the request path is direct HTTP/1.1 SSE or gRPC/HTTP2 proxied?
maria: It's gRPC over HTTP/2 via their envoy gateway -> our LB -> hosted inference. They call the streaming /generate endpoint with mode=json and a long streamed object. They attached a minimal repro (see below).
maria: repro snippet they sent:
```bash
# client uses grpcurl to stream and then resets connection after 7s
grpcurl -d '{"prompt":"keep streaming long json","mode":"json"}' 
  -plaintext 
  -import-path proto/ 
  -proto inference.proto 
  localhost:443 InferenceService.StreamGenerate
# then ctrl-c or reset TCP from client side
```
liam: Can you paste the server-side tail from the request trace? need to confirm whether final chunk contained a partial object (like missing trailing brace) or we cut at frame boundary.
maria: pasted a short excerpt from our streaming payload (trimmed):
```
data: {"records":[{"id":1,"text":"hello"},{"id":2,"text":"world"},
  {"id":3,"text":"incomplete"
# << stream terminated here (no closing ] or })
```
kevin: ok so client-initiated reset removes stream mid-object. Our streaming path currently flushes partial frames without inserting a termination token when gRPC/HTTP2 FIN arrives. That aligns with the customer's parser error.
eng-oncall: any sign of auth token refresh happening midstream? we've had reports where a 401 triggers a reconnect and the client resets the upstream stream.
maria: customer says their auth middleware did attempt refresh ~5s in on some runs. They see an initial 200 with token, then a short 401 on a follow-up background call which triggers their gateway to reset the call. They provided an envoy access log showing a 200 then a RST_STREAM.
liam: interesting. Two parallel issues: (1) premature stream reset leaving incomplete JSON; (2) billing surface — they were billed for tokens emitted before reset. We need to confirm charge policy for partial responses.
kevin: short-term workaround: switch client to newline-delimited JSON mode (ndjson) or parse by streaming decoder that tolerates partial last object and retries. Server-side long-term: ensure we emit a final 'end' event or close object atomically when a client reset is detected; also consider emitting an explicit "finished":false flag in the trailing frame so parsers can detect truncation.
maria: customer asked for repro steps we can run internally. I'll try to reproduce in staging with grpcurl and a simulated RST_STREAM from an nginx proxy. Will post logs.
eng-oncall: opened internal ticket RED-INC-12345 and linked customer case CS-9876. tagging @kevin @liam for follow-up. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Recorded incident RED-INC-12345, severity=prod-impacting, owner=eng-oncall, linked_cases=["CS-9876"].
kevin: thx. if you can capture the final 2KB of the stream and the proxy-level tcpdump that'll help. Also ask customer whether they want a credit for partial responses — advise support to hold on credits until we confirm root cause.
maria: will collect traces and ping here with upload link. For now I've given the customer the NDJSON workaround and asked them to hold on retry logic.
liam: one more note — if the client resets but we can detect it before buffer flush, we could avoid counting incomplete output for billing. Filing a billing policy question to finance after reproduction.
maria: ack, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short repro gist and staging trace later today.
